topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, adverse effects, and resistance mechanisms of traditional cancer treatments including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit cancer-specific weaknesses such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the targeting of oncogenic driver mutations and kinases along with the pathways leading to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic antibodies designed to target tumor surface markers directly or deliver attached cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Immunotherapy and T-Cell-Directed Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the relationship between the immune system and tumors, exploring methods to reactivate or genetically engineer T cells for cancer treatment.

topics.label: Therapeutic Challenges, Progress, and Future Outlook
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review clinical progress, current systemic challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and future directions in cancer treatment.
